browser: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/152.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
how: A real Chrome window driven step by step: the app's own bundled @rayfold/client talking to a running Rayfold server. Sign-in, search, opening a book, buying and paying were done with real clicks and typing; later runs repeated the same steps through the page's own forms and buttons.
dataset: The full Project Gutenberg catalogue: 78,086 real books by 26,263 authors, plus the demo's 4 seed books.

flows.step: Sign in with a session cookie

flows.result: 6 matches in 53 ms, including the French translation in three volumes.
Title, author with life dates 1797-1851, 25 books by the author, live stock 1,000,000, all in one request.
Order o1 PLACED. A second tab showing the same book received stock 999,999 over WebSocket without any HTTP request.
o1 PAID. The whole session so far used 8 HTTP requests and received 20,904 bytes.

crossSite.from: http://localhost:4611, a page on another origin. It shares the host with the demo, so the browser sends the SameSite=Lax session cookie with every attempt.

attempts.attempt: POST a placeOrder batch to /rayfold as text/plain, with the cookie (a request browsers send without asking)
attempts.observed: sent; the response is opaque to this page (opaque)

attempts.attempt: POST the same batch as application/rayfold+json, with the cookie (needs a CORS preflight)
attempts.observed: the browser blocked it: Failed to fetch

attempts.attempt: Submit an HTML form to POST /orders/o2/pay (pays the visitor's unpaid order)
attempts.observed: form submitted; the result page is cross-origin and unreadable

attempts.attempt: Open a WebSocket to /rayfold/ws (the browser attaches the cookie) and send placeOrder
POST MCP tools/call placeOrder to /mcp as text/plain, with the cookie
attempts.observed: sent; the response is opaque to this page (opaque)

attempts.attempt: Read the visitor's orders from /rayfold (a safe read, with the cookie)
attempts.observed: the browser blocked it: Failed to fetch

outcome: Run 1: before the attempts alice had one unpaid order, o1. After them the store still held exactly o1, still PLACED, and the stock was unchanged: no attempt placed or paid anything.
Run 2 (with the proxy origin allowed): the target was alice's unpaid order o2. Afterwards o2 was still PLACED and no new order existed: allowing one origin did not open the demo to others.

proxy.setup: Behind a proxy that rewrites Host (as nginx proxy_pass does), with no allowed origins
proxy.result: Search and the book page work (safe reads). Buying is refused with 403 "Origin http://localhost:4612 is not allowed", the WebSocket is refused, and no order is created.
Buy, pay and a second buy work through the proxy, the WebSocket opens through it, and a tab on the direct origin received both stock changes live.

foundAndFixed: Safe reads through a Host-rewriting proxy were refused together with writes. Safe requests (QUERY, or POST with Rayfold-Safe) are now exempt from the Origin check in both runtimes, since they cannot change data; writes still need the origin to be allowed.
The demo page's book panel ignored the hidden attribute (a CSS rule overrode it).
